title: An angklung melody is often split among several players
body: An Indonesian angklung contains two to four bamboo tubes suspended in a frame. Shaking it produces its pitch, so several people can take turns sounding their instruments to make a melody.
takeaway: A tune becomes an exercise in timing together when each player supplies only part of it.
source: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Indonesian Angklung (2010)
visual: hands shaking a bamboo angklung within a group of musicians

title: Panama's pintao hat combines several fibre-working techniques
body: Making a traditional pintao hat involves preparing plant fibres, colouring some of them and weaving them into patterned strips. Artisans then assemble the strips into the hat's striped form.
takeaway: The pattern belongs to the fibres and weave, rather than being printed onto a finished hat.
source: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Pintao Hat Weaving (2017)
visual: a striped woven Panamanian hat beside loose plant fibres

title: Uzbek palov is cooked for gatherings as well as daily meals
body: In Uzbekistan, palov combines rice, meat, vegetables and spices. Communities prepare it for ordinary meals and for shared events, including weddings and occasions when people support neighbours in need.
takeaway: A large dish that can be portioned out becomes a practical way to host a gathering.
source: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Palov Culture and Tradition (2016)
visual: a large cooking pot of rice and vegetables being served onto a platter
